## Sales data: pivot-table practice

In the first part, we work with the `Sales.xlsx` dataset:

```{python}
import pandas as pd
sales = pd.read_excel("Sales.xlsx")
```

### Summarize turnover by region

Calculate the total turnover in each region.

::: {.sol}
```{python}
pd.pivot_table(
    sales,
    index="Region",
    values="Turnover",
    aggfunc="sum",
)
```
:::

### Filter to actual sales

The dataset includes both actual and target values. Calculate total turnover by region for actual sales only.

::: {.sol}
```{python}
pd.pivot_table(
    sales.loc[sales["Category"] == "Actual"],
    index="Region",
    values="Turnover",
    aggfunc="sum",
)
```
:::

### Apply multiple aggregation functions

For actual sales, calculate the sum, mean, and standard deviation of turnover by region.

::: {.sol}
```{python}
pd.pivot_table(
    sales.loc[sales["Category"] == "Actual"],
    index="Region",
    values="Turnover",
    aggfunc=["sum", "mean", "std"],
)
```
:::

### Add products as a column dimension

Show the sum of turnover by region and product, first for the entire dataset and then for actual sales only.

::: {.sol}
```{python}
pd.pivot_table(
    sales,
    index="Region",
    columns="Product",
    values="Turnover",
    aggfunc="sum",
)
```

```{python}
pd.pivot_table(
    sales.loc[sales["Category"] == "Actual"],
    index="Region",
    columns="Product",
    values="Turnover",
    aggfunc="sum",
)
```
:::

### Combine filters

Calculate actual turnover by region and product for 2020. Parenthesize each Pandas comparison before combining conditions with `&`.

::: {.sol}
```{python}
pd.pivot_table(
    sales.loc[(sales["Category"] == "Actual") & (sales["Year"] == 2020)],
    index="Region",
    columns="Product",
    values="Turnover",
    aggfunc="sum",
)
```
:::

### Add totals and plot the pivot table

Store the pivot table in a DataFrame, add a total row, and make a bar chart. `margins=True` is an alternative way to include totals.

::: {.sol}
```{python}
pivot_df = pd.pivot_table(
    sales.loc[(sales["Category"] == "Actual") & (sales["Year"] == 2020)],
    index="Region",
    columns="Product",
    values="Turnover",
    aggfunc="sum",
)
pivot_df.loc["Total"] = pivot_df.sum()
pivot_df
```

```{python}
#| fig-align: center
pivot_df.plot(kind="bar")
```
:::

### Use multiple row dimensions

Create a hierarchical row index using year and region, with products as columns (remember to remove the year filter).

::: {.sol}
```{python}
pd.pivot_table(
    sales.loc[sales["Category"] == "Actual"],
    index=["Year", "Region"],
    columns="Product",
    values="Turnover",
    aggfunc="sum",
)
```
:::

## Insurance: pivot-table exercise

```{python}
insurance = pd.read_excel("insurance.xlsx")
```

### 1. Average insured value per state

::: {.sol}
```{python}
pd.pivot_table(
    insurance,
    index="State",
    values="InsuredValue",
    aggfunc="mean",
)
```
:::

### 2. Average insured value by state and location

Note: `fill_value=0` replaces missing cells in the result with zero.

::: {.sol}
```{python}
pd.pivot_table(
    insurance,
    index="State",
    columns="Location",
    values="InsuredValue",
    aggfunc="mean",
    fill_value=0,
)
```
:::

### 3. Flood or earthquake coverage, by state and region

Keep contracts with either flood or earthquake coverage, then calculate the average insured value for each state and region.

::: {.sol}
```{python}
pd.pivot_table(
    insurance.loc[(insurance["Flood"] == "Y") | (insurance["Earthquake"] == "Y")],
    index="State",
    columns="Region",
    values="InsuredValue",
    aggfunc="mean",
    fill_value=0,
)
```
:::

### 4. Flood and earthquake coverage, by state and construction

Keep only contracts with both coverages, then calculate the average insured value.

::: {.sol}
```{python}
pd.pivot_table(
    insurance.loc[(insurance["Flood"] == "Y") & (insurance["Earthquake"] == "Y")],
    index="State",
    columns="Construction",
    values="InsuredValue",
    aggfunc="mean",
    fill_value=0,
)
```
:::

### 5. Total insured value by location, business type, and region

::: {.sol}
```{python}
pd.pivot_table(
    insurance,
    index=["Location", "BusinessType"],
    columns="Region",
    values="InsuredValue",
    aggfunc="sum",
    fill_value=0,
)
```
:::

### 6. Add a total row

::: {.sol}
```{python}
insurance_pivot = pd.pivot_table(
    insurance,
    index=["Location", "BusinessType"],
    columns="Region",
    values="InsuredValue",
    aggfunc="sum",
    fill_value=0,
)
insurance_pivot.loc["Total"] = insurance_pivot.sum()
insurance_pivot
```

Another option is to use the built-in `margins=True` option.

```{python}
pd.pivot_table(
    insurance,
    index=["Location", "BusinessType"],
    columns="Region",
    values="InsuredValue",
    aggfunc="sum",
    fill_value=0,
    margins=True,
)
```

:::

### 7. Plot contract counts by location and state

::: {.sol}
```{python}
#| fig-align: center
insurance_counts = pd.pivot_table(
    insurance,
    index="Location",
    columns="State",
    values="InsuredValue",
    aggfunc="count",
    fill_value=0,
)
insurance_counts.plot(kind="bar")
```
:::
